newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Dollar ends Asia session firm, waits for U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Dollar ends Asia session firm, waits for U.S. data.

text.p: The U.S. dollar ended the Asian session slightly firmer against the German mark on Thursday, but dealers said activity would remain light until the release of U.S. trade data at 1330 GMT.
"There won't be any big one-way movement today. It'll be stuck in a range until New York," one dealer said.
Expectations of a US$10.7-billion U.S. trade deficit in January will cap U.S. dollar strength at 123 yen following a move to 123.10 early in the Asian session, dealers said.
Singapore dealers were not expecting any major moves on the data. "The market doesn't have any big positions now. Everyone's squared up," one dealer said.
The market failed to react to Germany's cost of living data for February, with the dollar trapped at about 1.6800 marks.
"It's range-bound, dull, boring, whatever. Rather be in the pub," said one trader.
But Singapore dealers said the dollar could be bought up against the mark, especially if it managed to breach 1.6880, where there was talk of stop-loss buy orders.

Generally, the market was extremely quiet with Tokyo markets closed for Vernal Equinox day. The only activity was on the sterling crosses, where strong economic data in the U.K. and stop-loss buying in a thin market sparked an early buying spree, but it quickly fizzled.
One Hong Kong-based analyst said the Rubgy Sevens tournament would ensure that Hong Kong's foreign exchange market would remain quiet from noon on Friday.
"Many, many people are going to go away for lunch and not come back," he said.
